core_obligations: Record that the first condition implies the second (proof line 2399).

From the second to the third: for a finite purely inseparable extension the spectrum of O_{X,x} tensor_k k' is a single point, so that ring is local and is the local ring at the unique point above x, hence regular by hypothesis, which is the definition of geometric regularity (proof lines 2400-2410).

From the third to the first: for an arbitrary field extension k', surjectivity of the base change gives a point x' above x and the local ring there is a localization of O_{X,x} tensor_k k', hence regular (proof lines 2413-2420).
proof_roadmap: Second to third via uniqueness of the point above x (proof lines 2400-2410).
Third to first via localizations of the tensor product (proof lines 2413-2420).
difficulty_reason: For a locally Noetherian scheme X over k and a point x, the lemma proves the equivalence of geometric regularity at x, regularity of the local rings at all points above x after every finite purely inseparable base change, and geometric regularity of the local ring O_{X,x} over k (statement lines 2381-2396). The proof is a short cycle. From the second condition to the third, the author observes that localizing a finite purely inseparable extension keeps the spectrum a single point, so the tensor product O_{X,x} tensor_k k' is local and equals the local ring at the unique point above x, which is regular by hypothesis (proof lines 2400-2410). From the third to the first, an arbitrary field extension is used: surjectivity of the base change gives a point x' above x, and the local ring there is a localization of O_{X,x} tensor_k k', hence regular (proof lines 2413-2420). The first condition implies the second by definition. The claim is H2: three short steps whose content is the uniqueness of the point above x under a purely inseparable extension and the localization description of the local ring there.
